intent.note: Task clause: 'The nt branch of _shim_dir and of the k15 working shim writes .cmd files and is untested on Windows ... a .cmd found by shutil.which and run without a shell, and a cmd shim that forwards %* to sys.executable, are assumptions'. Resolution asked: 'Confirm on the first windows CI run ... If k13-k15 go red there, build the shims as .bat or add the extension to PATHEXT'. The diff pulls the nt/posix spelling into pure _shim_spec/_passthrough_spec plus one _write_shim used by both _shim_dir and k15 (tools/check-git-pipeline.py, _interpreter_cases now calls _write_shim(working, _passthrough_spec(...))), pins the bytes on every platform (k18 nt: .cmd name, CRLF on every line, exit code 7 not fixed 1, quoted forwarder target with %*; k19 posix unchanged; k20 _shim_dir read back in binary equals the spec), and adds Windows-only k21-k24 that ask the real machine each assumption (which/PATHEXT finds the .cmd; list-argv run returns exit 3 and 0; forwarder passes the -c probe with space/semicolon/parens and prints 'ran'; forwarder exit 5 comes back). The executor's decision not to pre-emptively switch to .bat/PATHEXT is consistent with the 'if red' condition in the resolution. The claim describes the diff: file is the only one touched, the helper names and k-labels match, and I ran `python3 tools/check-git-pipeline.py --selftest` once in the task tree: ALL PASS 21/21 with k18-k20 PASS and one 'k21-k24 SKIPPED HERE' PASS line, stderr empty. What the diff cannot do is the 'confirm on Windows CI' half; that remains owed to the owner's Windows run, as the executor says. Windows judgement by reading: k21-k24 are not vacuous. If the shim is not found or has the wrong extension k21 (and k22, whose run falls to code None) goes red; a wrong exit code goes red in k22 (3 and 0 are distinguishable from a launch failure, which yields None); a dropped %* makes k23's output not equal 'ran'; a forwarder that swallows the target's status makes k24 see 0 instead of 5. Mechanics I checked from CPython behaviour: shutil.which returns dir\python3.CMD (case-insensitive compare used), CreateProcess wraps a .cmd's command line in cmd /c "..." so a quoted shim path plus a quoted -c argument survives quote stripping, and `cmd /c` of a batch file ends with the errorlevel of its last command or `exit /b N`. PowerShell command: `python ... | Select-String ...; $LASTEXITCODE` reports python's exit code, since $LASTEXITCODE holds the exit code of the last native program and Select-String is a cmdlet that does not set it; the selftest writes PASS/FAIL/ALL PASS/SELFTEST FAILED lines to stdout (stderr was empty on a green run), so the pattern sees them. I could not confirm this from the PowerShell docs here (no pwsh on this machine, no web tool); it rests on the documented about_Automatic_Variables description and on how the construct behaves. Known, acknowledged gap: a Windows TEMP path containing a space is not probed by any case.
